title: Logan Paul Lost $3.5 Million on Fake First-Edition Pokémon Cards
verified_facts: Box contained 1991 G.I. Joe trading cards instead of Pokémon Base Set
Seller Bolillo Lajan San reimbursed Logan Paul
Authentication was conducted by Baseball Card Exchange (BBCE)

title: Did Logan Paul Buy a Fake $3.5 Million Pokémon Box? The Evidence Explored
author: Jon Sahagian (WaterPokemonMaster)
verified_facts: Origin account on Canadian eBay was 'number1pokemonmaster'
Seller changed usernames and gave contradictory estate sale stories
Box tape and barcode labels did not match verified 1999 WotC shipping cases

title: Investigative Video Series: The Logan Paul $3.5M Sealed Case Investigation
creator: Rattle Pokémon
verified_facts: Frame-by-frame forensic analysis of BBCE authentication video
Demonstration of cardboard tape weathering and replacement seams
Analysis of BBCE's lack of prior vintage sealed Pokémon case expertise

title: I Lost $3,500,000 On Fake Pokémon Cards
creator: Logan Paul
verified_facts: Physical opening recorded in Chicago with BBCE owner Steve Hart
First booster box inspection revealed warped curvature and non-factory glue
Packs were verified as G.I. Joe Series 2 (1991)
Steve Hart publicly acknowledged the error on camera
